correctness.rationale: Independently enumerated allowed sources via separated one-positions and all same-weight receivers via unrestricted position subsets. Adjacent-swap distance is L1 on sorted positions: each swap moves one coordinate by one, and moving toward targets can always proceed by the leftmost required left move (or rightmost required right move). The complete ball condition is distance <=1; the confusability condition for distinct sources is distance <=2. Reconstructed 40 graphs, computed size and counts by disjoint branching on the first chosen element of a closed neighborhood or none, and verified the 40 listed codebooks and all exact sparse rational packing/cover weights by full receiver incidence. The ten (M,P,N) triples agree exactly with the repaired table. The only fractional excesses are at (n,k)=(7,2),(9,4),(10,2), equal to 1/5, 1/5 and 1/3. Independently counted reversal-fixed maxima by weighted independent sets on compatible reversal orbits, excluding internal-conflict orbits and comparing the orbit-graph maximum with the ordinary maximum. The fixed counts were 4 and 0 at 7 and 8, and Burnside gives 30 and 12. For the added shortening, shifting the sorted coordinate a_i to a_i−i maps the separated source subsets bijectively to length n−k+1 unrestricted subsets of weight k, preserving the L1 distance and intertwining reversal. Strict received coordinates after shifting give exactly the shorter unrestricted constraints. A reachable weak tuple has a single repeated pair (x,x), with at most two strict sources by replacing it by (x−1,x) or (x,x+1); if both are valid they lie in the row at the strict tuple with pair (x−1,x+1). With one source its own row dominates. Thus the remaining rows are redundant by nonnegativity. This verifies the LP equivalence analytically and it was also rechecked for every finite block in the profile. Weight zero is the trivial singleton throughout. The repair does not change any theorem or certificate value; it changes the stated prior coverage and supplies the exact equivalence supporting that correction.
residual_risks: The shorter-problem equivalence holds generally, but no general formula for its fractional or counting invariants is proved. Reversal counts are certified only for 7 and 8, not all ten lengths.

originality.rationale: Pass applies only to the repaired contribution: exact fractional packing and maximizing-codebook data through length ten, the first gap and rebound, and the specified reversal counts. Under a verified shortening isomorphism the whole integer-size sequence follows from published fixed-weight data, so the repair credits it as baseline, not novelty. The same isomorphism translates the remaining claims to unrestricted shorter fractional and counting problems; the inspected strongest exact prior tables contain integer sizes, not those invariants. Distinct same-date records were compared by their channel and source, not excluded by date.
residual_risks: The search for distinct published fractional or optimizer tables is bounded, not proof of absence. Unindexed unrestricted fixed-weight computations could cover portions of the survivor. No separate novelty is attributed to known integer capacities or to routine shortening itself.

Prior integer-only tables compared under shortening
value.rationale: After removing the covered integer profile as a contribution, this still gives the first boundary at which the natural complete-output LP ceases to be exact, demonstrates that tightness returns and is not monotone even in the initial range, locates the responsible weight blocks, and counts optimum choices and reversal classes in the exceptional lengths. This is a finite benchmark for certifying and classifying optima, not a renaming of the known integer values. The small fractional excess is meaningful because the target is the exact tightness property, not improvement in an engineering metric.
residual_risks: No integer-rounding failure, asymptotic gap or general capacity theorem follows. The census is for the stated range, with reversals only at seven and eight.
